message.text: Is there a version of this library that's supported?

reply.text:
Which library do you mean (JWT, Spring Security, jjwt, other)? 

Common choices and supported versions that fit the code shown:
- Spring Boot: 2.7.x (maintenance) or 3.1.x (current stable). Pick the Boot major that matches your Java version (Boot 3 requires Java 17+).
- Spring Security: 5.7.x for Boot 2.7, 6.1+ for Boot 3.x.
- JWT libraries:
  - `io.jsonwebtoken:jjwt` family — use `jjwt-api`/`jjwt-impl`/`jjwt-jackson` at 0.11.5 (current stable).
  - `com.nimbusds:nimbus-jose-jwt` — commonly used and actively maintained (match the latest 9.x series).
- Password hashing: use Spring Security `PasswordEncoder` from the matching Spring Security version (no separate version).

To confirm what's supported for your project, open `pom.xml` or `build.gradle` and share the dependency entries or the project SDK/Boot version.

That import is provided by Spring Security; your project is missing the dependency (or Eclipse hasn't refreshed). Add Spring Security (recommended: the Spring Boot starter) and refresh the project.

Explanation: `org.springframework.security.crypto.password.PasswordEncoder` is in Spring Security. Add `spring-boot-starter-security` (or `spring-security-core`) to `pom.xml` or `build.gradle`, then update dependencies in Eclipse.

Maven (`pom.xml`) example:
```xml
<!-- Add inside <dependencies> -->
<dependency>
  <groupId>org.springframework.boot</groupId>
  <artifactId>spring-boot-starter-security</artifactId>
</dependency>
```

Gradle (`build.gradle`) example:
```groovy
dependencies {
  implementation 'org.springframework.boot:spring-boot-starter-security'
}
```

If you prefer the minimal artifact:
```xml
<!-- Maven -->
<dependency>
  <groupId>org.springframework.security</groupId>
  <artifactId>spring-security-core</artifactId>
  <version>6.1.6</version> <!-- match your Spring Boot / Java version -->
</dependency>
```

After adding the dependency:
- For Maven: right-click project in Eclipse -> `Maven` -> `Update Project` (or run `mvn clean install`).
- For Gradle: refresh the Gradle project in Eclipse (or run `./gradlew build`).

If you use `module-info.java`, also add the appropriate `requires` entry for Spring Security modules.

Those imports are part of Spring Security. Add the Spring Security dependency that matches your Spring Boot / Java version and refresh dependencies in Eclipse.

Explanation: use `spring-boot-starter-security` (no explicit version if you use the Spring Boot parent), or add `spring-security-core` / matching Spring Security 6.x if not using Boot starters.

```xml
<!-- xml -->
<!-- Maven (add inside `dependencies` in `pom.xml`) -->
<dependency>
  <groupId>org.springframework.boot</groupId>
  <artifactId>spring-boot-starter-security</artifactId>
</dependency>

<!-- Or, if not using Spring Boot starter, add Spring Security core (match version to your Spring Boot / Java): -->
<dependency>
  <groupId>org.springframework.security</groupId>
  <artifactId>spring-security-core</artifactId>
  <version>6.1.6</version> <!-- use 6.x for Spring Boot 3 / Java 17+; use 5.7.x for Boot 2.7 -->
</dependency>

<!-- Gradle (add to `dependencies` in `build.gradle`) -->
// implementation 'org.springframework.boot:spring-boot-starter-security'
```

Steps:
- If Maven: right-click project in Eclipse -> Maven -> Update Project (or run `mvn clean install`).
- If Gradle: Refresh Gradle project (or run `./gradlew build`).
- Ensure Java and Spring Boot versions are compatible (Spring Security 6 requires Java 17+ and Spring Boot 3.x).
- If you use `module-info.java`, add the appropriate `requires` entries for the Spring Security modules you use.
